introduction.text: The Mausoleo di Campo Barbarico is a Roman funerary building of the "tomb with temple" type located in Rome's Municipio VII, notable for its 2nd‑century construction, later use as a hay barn, and 16th‑century drawings that reveal its rich interior decoration.

history.description: Construction of the mausoleum in the 2nd century AD using opus latericium.
The site was used as a Gothic camp by the forces of Vitiges in 539 during the siege of Rome.
First documented description by an anonymous artist in 1570, producing drawings preserved at Windsor.
Continued use as a hay barn until the end of the 19th century.
Consolidation and restoration work began in 1974.
After abandonment and seismic collapses, the mausoleum was partially reconstructed in the Middle Ages and served as a hay barn until the end of the 19th century.

design.description: The mausoleum has a rectangular plan measuring 8.30 by 9.90 meters, with an entrance facing Via Latina.
The interior consists of a single rectangular space covered by a barrel vault with coffering; only the vault's base remains.
Lateral walls feature three orders of niches and arches; the back wall has two registers with a central niche and staircases leading to a double tympanum.
The exterior, especially the main facade, was partially reconstructed after collapses, but originally it was rather plain.

art.description: The mausoleum's interior decoration was rich, as evidenced by 16th‑century drawings and some surviving fresco fragments.
Surviving fresco fragments on the back wall indicate the presence of painted decoration.
